brief: Matches you with fresh roasted bags from small roasters, subscription with a quiz. Bags run $15-25. Looking for home brewers and WFH folks.

profile.business_summary: A personalized coffee subscription service that matches home brewers and WFH professionals with freshly roasted coffee bags from small-batch roasters using an onboarding quiz.
stated_claims: Matches you with fresh roasted bags from small roasters

relevant_tags.why: The business model is explicitly subscription-based.
The core product is coffee, which is a beverage.
Coffee beans are a standard pantry staple for home brewers.
The service uses a quiz to match users with specific coffee bags.
Coffee is a high-frequency grocery item.
Targeting home brewers who use kitchen coffee-making equipment.

persona_conflicts.evidence: The service requires a 'quiz' to match users with coffee bags, which busy parents might find tedious.
The advertiser describes the service as a 'subscription with a quiz'.

note_signals.why: Pantrygood has values-driven, organic/natural pantry shoppers who appreciate premium, small-batch grocery items.
Hearthstone Goods attracts kitchen buyers and home cooks who likely brew coffee at home.
Strandlab's audience is highly motivated by personalization and already comfortable with quiz-based onboarding.
Pop & Sip has strong overlap with premium grocery and beverage buyers.
Kitchenly's subscription-friendly, food-interested audience is ideal for a coffee subscription.
Cloudfoot's tech-adjacent urban professional audience strongly overlaps with the 'WFH folks' target demographic.

profile.gate_reason: The product, pricing, subscription model, and target audience are clearly defined and highly suitable for the DTC network.
clarifying_questions: Is there a one-time purchase option available, or is it strictly subscription-only?
What is the typical shipping frequency for the subscription (e.g., weekly, monthly)?
Do you offer free shipping on subscription bags, or is there an additional shipping fee?

config.advertiser_summary: A personalized coffee subscription service that matches home brewers and WFH professionals with freshly roasted coffee bags from small-batch roasters using an onboarding quiz.

assumptions: subscription: assumed 4.0 orders per customer over ~6 months.
No target CPA/ROAS or margin given; assumed 50% gross margin (typical for beverages). Give a target CPA to replace this.
Target CPA = 70% of max affordable CAC ($20 x 50% margin x 4.0 orders = $40.00).

pricing.rationale: Acquisition goal with no conversion history: pay per click. Max CPC = target CPA $28.00 x click-to-purchase rate (1.6%-5.6% for beverages). Clicks are observable without trusting a pixel, so both sides can verify billing.
pricing.tcpa_unlock: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded; until then Disco can't predict conversion rate for this brand.

budget.pacing: even daily pacing; pause a host if CPA > 2.0x target after 150 clicks

allocations.rationale: score 0.37 -> relative fit x1.40 on CTR/CVR; max bid $1.25 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%
score 0.33 -> relative fit x1.33 on CTR/CVR; max bid $1.19 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%
score 0.31 -> relative fit x1.28 on CTR/CVR; max bid $1.15 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%
score 0.25 -> relative fit x1.14 on CTR/CVR; max bid $1.02 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%

warnings: No budget given: recommending $1,630, the smallest budget that buys 300 clicks per host.

phases.name: learning
phases.rule: bid = start bid per host (70% of break-even); pacing adjustment only
phases.why: stable bids so measured CTR/CVR aren't confounded by bid changes

phases.name: enhanced_cpc
phases.until: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded; until then Disco can't predict conversion rate for this brand.
phases.rule: bid = start bid x conversion_likelihood x pacing, clamped to [floor, max bid]
phases.why: spend more on shoppers who look likely to buy, never above break-even

phases.name: target_cpa
phases.rule: Disco bids automatically to hit $28.00 CPA
phases.why: only once Disco can predict this brand's conversion rate

adjustments.reason: Bid higher when the shopper looks like a high converter: their persona match for this campaign vs the host's average shopper (from the serve-time persona posterior).
Under-delivering vs the daily plan -> bid up a little; over-delivering -> bid down.

bid_strategy.rationale: Start below break-even and fixed so the first two weeks measure the hosts, not the bidder; then bid per shopper within a hard ceiling (max CPC = target CPA x CVR), so a single click can never cost more than it's expected to earn.
